name: Model 2

families.name: Entity registry
families.description: What exists and who owns what, on any date. Facts are never overwritten: a change adds a new version and closes the old one.
families.note: Every table here also has six history columns: valid_from and valid_to (when the fact was true; valid_to excluded), recorded_at and superseded_at (when it was learned and replaced), source and decided_by. Every table here belongs to one world, by folder: its keys are unique only within that world, so a row's full key is (world_id, its key). Entity and observation ids repeat across synthetic worlds of one generator. The world's id is checked whenever the world is loaded.

families.name: Observations
families.description: Every published reading, one row per value, plus the catalog of reading types and the census counts.
families.note: Every table here belongs to one world, by folder: its keys are unique only within that world, so a row's full key is (world_id, its key). Entity and observation ids repeat across synthetic worlds of one generator. The world's id is checked whenever the world is loaded.

families.name: Sector input bundle
families.description: Each sector's drivers and statistics as ensemble draws, delivered by an outside source once per run date and never changed afterwards.
families.note: Each delivery carries a manifest listing its tables with their schema versions, row counts and checksums. Every table here belongs to one world, by folder: its keys are unique only within that world, so a row's full key is (world_id, its key). Entity and observation ids repeat across synthetic worlds of one generator. The world's id is checked whenever the world is loaded.

families.name: Configuration
families.description: The settings people choose to steer the model: run and estimation settings, observation noise and calibrations, sector settings, priors and series mappings.

families.name: Parameter fitting
families.description: The parameters estimated for each sector and quarter, with a record of each fit.
families.note: Estimated once a quarter for each sector; every run in that quarter reuses them.

families.name: Synthetic truth
families.description: The true values behind a synthetic world: hidden states, parameters and drivers. Present only in synthetic worlds; the model never sees them.
families.note: Every table here belongs to one world, by folder: its keys are unique only within that world, so a row's full key is (world_id, its key). Entity and observation ids repeat across synthetic worlds of one generator. The world's id is checked whenever the world is loaded.

families.name: Run outputs
families.description: What each run produces for its run date. Tables marked published are delivered to users; the rest are kept for diagnosis.

families.name: Scores
families.description: How close each run came: errors and band coverage for every scored value, a record of each backtest, and one summary per backtest.
families.note: In a synthetic world the scores compare runs with the synthetic truth; scoring a real world against later publications is not built yet.

families.name: Catalog
families.description: A lasting record of every world, model version, fit and forecast, spanning all the other phases: worlds are recorded as they are built, fits and forecasts as they are made, and problems and fixes name the ones they are about. One record per item; records point to each other by id and say where the files they describe are. Every id is a UUID that says nothing about the record; readable names are separate fields.
families.note: Every record also has recorded_utc, when the catalog learned of it.

families.name: Problems, fixes and tests
families.description: What the evaluation of a forecast found wrong, the possible fixes for it, the fixes chosen to be tested and what each test found. Each record has an id that never changes and names the world, fit and forecast it is about. Later: the fixes good enough to deploy.
families.note: Every record also has recorded_utc, when it was first registered, and updated_utc, when its text last changed; the id never changes.
